content: Keep a detailed list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription medications as well as herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests and complete blood counts, should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically while taking it. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Take this medication by mouth with meals as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. For certain conditions, such as hydatid disease, your doctor may recommend taking this medication in treatment cycles (e.g., twice daily with meals for 28 days, followed by a 2-week break). Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) each day. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Other medications, such as corticosteroids or anti-seizure drugs, may also be prescribed for your condition. Avoid consuming grapefruit or grapefruit juice while using this medication unless your doctor or pharmacist advises otherwise, as grapefruit can increase the risk of side effects. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, or temporary hair loss. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking albendazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other benzimidazole anthelmintic drugs (e.g., mebendazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause liver problems. Limit alcoholic beverages while using this medication, as alcohol increases the risk of liver complications. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using albendazole, as it may harm an unborn baby. Your doctor will likely order a pregnancy test before starting this medication. Discuss reliable forms of birth control to use during treatment and for three days after the last dose. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. The information provided here is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
